# glinet_client_info (Resource)

Manages the name and the icon of a client device in the client list of the router, as the edit dialog of the clients page of the web UI does. The write was not tested on a router; the parameters come from the router's web UI. Create fails when the client list of the router has no client with the MAC address, because it is not known whether the router accepts a name or an icon for a MAC address that is not in the list. When the client goes out of the client list, refresh removes the resource from the state. The provider finds the client without letter case and writes the MAC address in the letter case of the client list. Import sets `mac` in the letter case of the client list. Destroy sets the name and the icon of the client back to automatic.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "glinet_client_info" "tablet" {
  mac   = "02:00:00:00:00:01"
  alias = "tablet"
  class = "pad"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `mac` (String) MAC address of the client, in lower case or upper case, for example `02:00:00:00:00:01`. A change of only the letter case changes only the state. Another change replaces the resource.

### Optional

- `alias` (String) Name of the client, at most 32 characters, without `,` and `"`. An empty string sets the name back to automatic: the router then shows the name that it found. When not set, the provider sends the name that the router has.
- `class` (String) Icon of the client. The web UI of firmware 4.8.3 offers `computer`, `phone`, `pad`, `camera`, `watch`, `laptop`, `printer`, `sound`, `television`, `smartappliances`, `games`, `gateway`, `nas`, `server` and `switch`. The provider does not limit the value to this list, because other firmware versions can have other icons. An empty string sets the icon back to automatic. When not set, the provider sends the icon that the router has.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# The import ID is the MAC address, in lower or upper case.
terraform import glinet_client_info.tablet 02:00:00:00:00:01
```
